In detail

This central district covers Syntagma, Omonoia, Monastiraki, Plaka, Kolonaki, Lycabettus, Exarchia, Koukaki, Ilisia and Makrygianni. It is genuinely two different areas after dark. Omonoia Square has a well-documented, ongoing open drug-dealing problem, with police arrests reported through 2025 and into 2026, including a June 2026 bust in which minors were used as runners. Exarchia has a long-running pattern of anarchist-police clashes and, separately, a June 2026 drug-related shooting that left one person dead. Pickpocketing targeting tourists is a recurring, widely reported issue around the metro system, Syntagma Square and Monastiraki. By contrast, Kolonaki, Plaka, Makrygianni and Koukaki are calm, affluent or tourist-oriented areas with no comparable pattern of documented incidents. Because the district mixes a serious, recurring night-time problem in specific pockets with genuinely quiet, upscale streets a few minutes away, day is rated yellow (pickpocketing risk) and night is rated red overall for the district. Sources checked: lawandorder.gr; todaypress.gr; GreekCityTimes; ProtoThema English; Athens-Times; The National Herald.
